positions.as_written: Set out the components and what each contributes.
Assess the pivot shift grade rather than anterior translation alone when the anterolateral side is in question, because that is the movement this complex controls.
Expect a high grade pivot shift to indicate injury here as well as to the cruciate.
Consider a lateral extra-articular procedure in a revision, in a high grade pivot shift, or in generalised laxity.
Avoid insisting on one component's primacy.
Treat the region as the unit of planning.
Treat the complex as the secondary rotational restraint whose role is revealed by cruciate failure.
Grade the pivot shift and record the grade, because it is the one examination finding that reflects this region.
Plan an anterolateral construct from the two reliable points, the supracondylar ridge and the tibia between Gerdy's tubercle and the fibular head.
Consider the indication rather than the anatomy when deciding whether to add a lateral procedure, since the anatomy supports it and the indication is what is argued.
